situation:
You are the marketing coordinator at SUNROW JUICE CO-OP, a chain of eighteen smoothie and juice bars owned by the people who work in them. Every full-time worker holds a share and votes at the annual meeting, and profits are paid out to members at year end. The board chair (judge), elected by the members, has asked you to bring a recommendation to a meeting this week.

Every cup the co-op sells carries the same brand promise: made from whole fruit, never concentrate. That promise, the open prep counters where customers watch the fruit go into the blender, and the member-owned sign in each window are what regulars name when they are asked why they choose SUNROW JUICE CO-OP over cheaper chains.

A spring whole-fruit promotion sold far more than the co-op had bought. Mango ran out in nine days, several bars served substitutes without saying so, and members heard about it from their own customers. PARKLINE MARKETS, a regional grocery chain, has since offered to carry a bottled SUNROW JUICE CO-OP line on four hundred shelves.

Signing with PARKLINE MARKETS would bring guaranteed revenue and money to buy fruit ahead of the next promotion, but the bottled line has to be shelf-stable, which means concentrate under the co-op's own name, and the grocery chain sets the packaging and the shelf price. Members would no longer vote on either one.

Turning the offer down and funding more fresh fruit out of the members' year-end payout keeps the promise on the cup and the vote with the members, but it costs members the payout they were counting on, and the promotion stays capped at what the co-op can buy. The board chair (judge) wants your reading of why customers buy here and a recommendation on the offer. The board chair (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the board chair (judge) of SUNROW JUICE CO-OP, elected by the members. Business background is the same as the situation above. You have to take an answer back to the members who own the co-op, you have read the offer from PARKLINE MARKETS, and you know the spring promotion ran out of mango in nine days. You want the marketing coordinator to tell you why customers buy here and to recommend whether the co-op should sign.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, what would tell us we made the right call?
If this turns out to be the wrong call, when would we find out?
